tob-10234: The Diamond Sutra is one of Buddhism’s most treasured texts: a dialogue in which the Buddha teaches that everything we see is like a dream, a bubble, a flash of lightning — empty of any lasting self. This insight lies at the heart of Mahayana Buddhism. William Gemmell’s translation presents the compact sutra; its 868 CE printed copy at Dunhuang is the oldest dated printed book known.
tob-9334: The Didache — the Teaching of the Twelve — is the oldest church handbook to survive, a first-century rule for washing, fasting, prayer, and the holy meal. Found in a Constantinople house of monks in 1873 by Bryennios, it startled the learned with its peep at earliest Christian wont. Short text; huge weight.
tob-4185-78134: The first volume of Goodwin’s five-book Plutarch opens the Moralia — pieces on rearing, on hearkening, on sifting flatterers from friends. These are antiquity’s kindliest self-betterment writings. The edition brought Plutarch the moralist to English readers.
tob-4134: Isaac Myer’s Qabbalah was America’s first weighty book on the Kabbalah — its teachings, story, and book-lore, drawn straight from Hebrew wells. Out in 1888, it opened Jewish holy-mystery to English readers. Scholars still cite Myer’s trail-work. It stays a honored first guide to the field.
tob-10034: Mackail’s Englishing of Virgil’s Field-Book gives the great tilling-poem — four books on tilth, trees, kine, and bees. Maecenas bade him write it, to heal Rome’s war-torn farms. The poem is the crown of Latin teaching-verse. This printing bears his praise of field-life to English readers.
a-popular-history-of-ireland-from-the-ea: This edition of Thomas D'Arcy McGee's beloved history brings Ireland's story — from misty origins to the winning of Catholic Emancipation — to a new generation of readers. McGee writes as both scholar and patriot, making centuries of struggle vivid and personal. An enduring, heartfelt telling of the Irish past.
arxiv-2605-08734: Fine-tuning giant models on a budget usually means LoRA, which trains small low-rank patches instead of updating every weight. The 2026 paper is optimization research for practitioners adapting large models cheaply.
arxiv-2605-08834: On February 27, 2023, a brilliant fireball streaked over northern Sweden — and cameras built to watch the aurora caught it. The paper turns a sky-watching accident into planetary science.
arxiv-2605-08934: Mechanistic interpretability reverse-engineers neural networks neuron by neuron; compositional interpretability asks how those pieces combine into larger meanings. arxiv-2605-09034: Zeroth-order optimization tunes models using only function values — no gradients — and spectral methods organize the search. Jiahe Chen and Ziye Ma accelerate it with partial orthogonalization drawn from power iteration. The 2026 paper is optimization for the gradient-free world.

arxiv-2605-09334: Mahler's conjecture — about the minimum volume of a convex body and its polar — is a crown jewel of convex geometry; the non-symmetric case in three dimensions is the frontier. plos-pone-0355934: Electrical grounding systems can be improved with biodegradable waste — turning trash into safety. plos-pone-0354134: Spotted wing drosophila — Drosophila suzukii — ravages fruit crops on schedules growers need to know. plos-pone-0354834: Detecting cardiac abnormalities from ECG — reliably and with calibrated confidence — could save lives at scale. plos-pone-0353934: Eritrea’s Asmara Belt — hunting volcanogenic massive sulfide minerals from space. This paper integrated Sentinel-2 imagery with geology data for VMS mineralization mapping.
